assumptions.condition: The vectors \(W_1,\ldots,W_T\) are independent and identically distributed under \(P\).
Conditional on \(X_t\) and \(\mathcal F_{t-1}\), the action \(A_t\) is drawn from the logged distribution \(\pi_t(\cdot\mid X_t,\mathcal F_{t-1})\) independently of \((Y_t(a))_{a\in\mathcal A}\).
For every \(a\in\mathcal A\), \(x\in\mathcal X\), and \(\eta\in\mathsf H\), the policy satisfies \(\Pi(a\mid x,\eta)\ge\varepsilon\).
The common envelope satisfies \(\sup_{a\in\mathcal A,\theta\in\Theta}\|g(a,X_t,Y_t(a);\theta)\|_2\le B\) almost surely.
constants: \(B<\infty\), fixed across every horizon and member law

assumptions.condition: The map \(\theta\mapsto g(a,x,y;\theta)\) is continuously differentiable on a common open neighborhood of \(\operatorname{conv}(\Theta)\), with \(\|\partial_\theta g(a,x,y;\theta)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le D_1\) there, and is twice continuously differentiable on the closed \(\rho\)-ball about \(\theta^*\), with \(\|\partial_\theta^2 g(a,x,y;\theta)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le D_2\) throughout that ball.
constants: \(D_1,D_2<\infty\) and \(\rho>0\), fixed across every horizon and member law
\(\kappa(u)>0\) for every \(u>0\), fixed across every horizon and member law

standard.name: Uniform separation of a Z-functional root

constants: \(s_\Theta>0\), fixed across every horizon and member law
\(h_->0\), fixed across every horizon and member law

assumptions.condition: The common policy modulus satisfies \(\sup_{a\in\mathcal A,x\in\mathcal X}|\Pi(a\mid x,\eta)-\Pi(a\mid x,\eta')|\le L_\Pi\|\eta-\eta'\|_2\) for all \(\eta,\eta'\in\mathsf H\).
constants: \(L_\Pi<\infty\), fixed across every horizon and member law

assumptions.condition: There exists a \(\sigma(\bigcup_{t\ge1}\mathcal F_t)\)-measurable \(\{1,\ldots,m\}\)-valued random variable \(J\) such that \(\eta_\infty=\bar\eta_J\) almost surely.

novel.justification: This atomic condition selects one of finitely many fixed terminal states without imposing pointwise convergence of the policy state.
This single Cesaro relation is the only path-approximation restriction and supplies a falsifiable common triangular-array modulus without imposing pointwise state convergence.

assumptions.condition: The common deterministic error envelope satisfies \(e_T=T^{-1/2}+r_T+\delta_T\to0\).

novel.justification: The combined envelope is a proposal-specific class-level restriction coupling sampling fluctuation, Cesaro attraction error, and attraction-tail probability. It is directly satisfied by immediately locking finite-state adaptive rules and can be audited from replicated policy paths; Mourrat supplies only the martingale central-limit ingredient used after this envelope is imposed.

assumptions.condition: The terminal covariance satisfies \(\Omega_\infty\succeq\omega_-I_d\) almost surely.
constants: \(\omega_->0\), fixed across every horizon and member law

novel.justification: A common almost-sure lower eigenvalue bound for the terminal random covariance is the proposal-specific uniform variance-growth primitive. The matching upper bound is derived from policy-wide overlap and the bounded score, not assumed.

definitions.name: finite-tail-attractor adaptive-experiment class
definitions.construction: For fixed \(m\), \(\bar\eta_1,\ldots,\bar\eta_m\), \(s_\eta\), \(p_-\), \(\varepsilon,B,D_1,D_2,h_-,L_\Pi,\omega_-,\kappa,s_\Theta,\rho\), and common sequences \((r_T,\delta_T)_{T\ge1}\), define \(\mathfrak P_T\) to be the set of laws \(P\) that, at horizon \(T\), satisfy every condition in \(\mathrm{ass:iid\text{-}full\text{-}data},\ldots,\mathrm{ass:basin\text{-}nondegeneracy}\) with these common objects, envelopes, and moduli. The fixed states obey \(\mathrm{ass:finite\text{-}attractor\text{-}separation}\), the terminal label and selected state obey \(\mathrm{ass:finite\text{-}tail\text{-}selection}\), every label obeys \(\mathrm{ass:basin\text{-}mass\text{-}floor}\), and the path approximation is supplied solely by \(\mathrm{ass:uniform\text{-}attraction\text{-}modulus}\). Thus \(\eta_\infty=\bar\eta_J\), every one of the \(m\) separated basins has mass at least \(p_-\), and the policy path is approximated by its selected attractor only through the uniform Cesaro inequality. Pointwise convergence of \(\eta_t\) is not imposed.

definitions.name: adaptive IPW-Z estimator
definitions.construction: First choose a measurable preliminary estimator \(\widetilde\theta_T\in\Theta\) satisfying \(\|G_T(\widetilde\theta_T)\|_2\le\inf_{\theta\in\Theta}\|G_T(\theta)\|_2+T^{-1/2}(r_T+\delta_T)\), using a fixed measurable tie-breaking rule. Define the compact correspondence \(\mathcal Z_T=\{\theta\in\Theta:G_T(\theta)=0,\ \|\theta-\widetilde\theta_T\|_2\le\rho/2\}\) and \(E_T=\{\mathcal Z_T\ne\varnothing\}\). Continuity of \(G_T\) on compact \(\Theta\) makes \(\mathcal Z_T\) compact, and its standard joint measurability permits a fixed measurable lexicographic compact-set selector. On \(E_T\), let \(\widehat\theta_T\) be that selected member of \(\mathcal Z_T\); on \(E_T^c\), set \(\widehat\theta_T=\widetilde\theta_T\).

definitions.name: bounded two-state separation witness
definitions.construction: For every \(T\ge2\), let \(P^{\dagger}\) be the law with \(K=3\), \(d=2\), \(\Theta=[-1,1]^2\), \(\theta^*=0\), a singleton \(\mathcal X\), and constant \(X_t\). Independently across \(t\) and between arms, let \(Y_t(1)\) be equiprobable on \(\{-\sqrt{2/5},\sqrt{2/5}\}\), let \(Y_t(2)\) be equiprobable on \(\{-\sqrt{1/2},\sqrt{1/2}\}\), and set \(Y_t(3)=0\). Set \(g(1,x,y;\theta)=(y-\theta_1,0)^\top\), \(g(2,x,y;\theta)=(0,y-\theta_2)^\top\), and \(g(3,x,y;\theta)=0\). Take \(m=2\), \(q=1\), \(\mathsf H=[0,1]\), \(\bar\eta_1=0\), \(\bar\eta_2=1\), and linearly interpolate the context-free policy between \(\Pi(\cdot\mid x,0)=(2/5,1/4,7/20)\) and \(\Pi(\cdot\mid x,1)=(2/5,1/6,13/30)\). Start at \(\eta_0=1/2\), set \(J=1\) if and only if \(A_1=1\), set \(J=2\) otherwise, define \(\eta_\infty=\bar\eta_J=J-1\), and put \(\eta_t=\eta_\infty\) for every \(t\ge1\).

definitions.name: terminal-representative covariance
definitions.construction:
For \(\eta\in\mathsf H\), define
\[
 \Gamma_P(\eta)=E_P\!\left[\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}
 \frac{g(a,X_t,Y_t(a);\theta^*)g(a,X_t,Y_t(a);\theta^*)^\top}
 {\Pi(a\mid X_t,\eta)}\right].
\]
For every \(j\in\mathcal J=\{1,\ldots,m\}\), set
\[
 p_j=P(J=j),\qquad
 \Omega_j=\Gamma_P(\bar\eta_j),\qquad
 V_j=H^{-1}\Omega_jH^{-\top}.
\]
Define
\[
 \Omega_J=\sum_{j=1}^m\mathbf1\{J=j\}\Omega_j,\qquad
 V_J=\sum_{j=1}^m\mathbf1\{J=j\}V_j,
\]
and set
\[
 \Omega_\infty=\Gamma_P(\eta_\infty),\qquad
 V_\infty=H^{-1}\Omega_\infty H^{-\top}.
\]
Under \(\mathrm{ass:finite\text{-}tail\text{-}selection}\), substitution of \(\eta_\infty=\bar\eta_J\) gives \(\Omega_\infty=\Omega_J\) and \(V_\infty=V_J\) almost surely.

definitions.name: event-truncated realized-QV sandwich
definitions.construction: Set \(\widehat\Omega_T=T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^T\widehat\xi_t\widehat\xi_t^\top\) and \(\mathcal E_T=\{\sigma_{\min}(\widehat H_T)\ge h_-/2,\ \lambda_{\min}(\widehat\Omega_T)\ge\omega_-/2\}\). Define \(\widehat V_T=\widehat H_T^{-1}\widehat\Omega_T\widehat H_T^{-\top}\) on \(\mathcal E_T\) and \(\widehat V_T=I_d\) on \(\mathcal E_T^c\).

definitions.name: bounded-noise Guo--Xu no-intercept recursion
definitions.construction: Fix \(K=2\), draw \(X_t\) independently and uniformly from \(\{-4,1\}\), and set \(Y_t(1)=1/2+\sigma_1R_{t,1}\) and \(Y_t(2)=1/12+\sigma_2R_{t,2}\), where the \(R_{t,a}\) are independent centered Rademacher innovations and \(\sigma_1,\sigma_2>0\) are arbitrary fixed constants declared as part of this bounded analogue; no numerical innovation variances are attributed to Guo and Xu. Keep their no-intercept working model, ridge constant \(\lambda=1\), unit-precision ridge initialization, and updates \(\Phi^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,a}=\Phi^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t-1,a}+\mathbf 1\{A_t=a\}X_t^2\), \(b^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,a}=b^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t-1,a}+\mathbf 1\{A_t=a\}X_tY_t\), and \(\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,a}=b^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,a}/\Phi^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,a}\). For \(\eta_0\in\mathsf K_{\mathrm{GX}}\), initialize \(Z^{\mathrm{GX}}_0=\iota_{\mathrm{GX}}(\eta_0)=(\eta_{0,1},\eta_{0,2},1,1)^\top\), equivalently \(\Phi^{\mathrm{GX}}_{0,a}=1\) and \(b^{\mathrm{GX}}_{0,a}=\eta_{0,a}\); the published initialization is the included case \(\eta_0=(0,0)^\top\). At occasion \(t\), break every exact index tie in favor of arm \(1\), maximize \(\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t-1,a}X_t+|X_t|\sqrt{q^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t-1,a}}\), and then assign the maximizing arm with probability \(0.99\) and the other arm with probability \(0.01\). The process of interest is the slope projection \((\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,1},\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,2})^\top\) of \(Z^{\mathrm{GX}}_t\), not a slope-only Markov chain.

definitions.name: bounded-recursion dynamics certification handle
definitions.construction: Write \(Z^{\mathrm{GX}}_t=(\beta_1,\beta_2,q_1,q_2)^\top\) for a current augmented state. Its induced armwise update is \(q_a^+=q_a/(1+\mathbf 1\{A=a\}q_aX^2)\) and \(\beta_a^+=(\beta_a+\mathbf 1\{A=a\}q_aXY(a))/(1+\mathbf 1\{A=a\}q_aX^2)\). The next clipped-UCB action uses \(\beta_aX+|X|\sqrt{q_a}\), so \(Z^{\mathrm{GX}}_t\), rather than its two-dimensional slope projection, is the time-homogeneous Markov state. For stochastic-approximation analysis, put \(D_{t,a}=\Phi^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,a}\), \(N_{t,a}=b^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,a}\), and, for \(t\ge1\), \(\Psi_t=(D_{t,1}/t,D_{t,2}/t,N_{t,1}/t,N_{t,2}/t)\). Analyze the exact \(1/(t+1)\) recursion for \(\Psi_t\) on an eventually compact region with both normalized Gram coordinates bounded away from zero. At the equal-slope surface, retain every limiting conditional-mean mode generated by the square-root UCB bonus: although the bonus is \(O(t^{-1/2})\), it can make the same arm greedy at both contexts inside an \(O(t^{-1/2})\) switching layer. Thus a closed convexified limiting graph must include these same-arm modes as well as the two opposite-context modes. Any differential-inclusion reduction must verify the closed-graph, compact-convex-value, boundedness, vanishing-perturbation, and martingale-tail conditions for this normalized recursion. Compact-uniform sequences \(r_T(K_0),\delta_T(K_0)\to0\) require a separate quantitative hitting or escape estimate and may not be inferred from pointwise convergence by a finite-cover argument.

statements.statement:
The common derivative and bounded-IPW envelopes imply
\[
 \|H\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le KD_1,
 \qquad
 \omega_-I_d\preceq\Omega_j\preceq(KB^2/\varepsilon)I_d
 \quad\text{for every }j\in\mathcal J=\{1,\ldots,m\}.
\]
The finite-tail-selection relation gives \(\Omega_\infty=\Omega_J\) and \(V_\infty=V_J\) almost surely. There is a finite constant \(C\), independent of \(T\) and \(P\), such that
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_T}E_P\!\left[
 \left\|T^{-1}\langle S\rangle_T-\Omega_J\right\|_{\mathrm{op}}\right]
 \le C(r_T+\delta_T).
\]
The preliminary estimator is uniformly consistent, \(G_T(\theta^*)=O_P(T^{-1/2})\), and \(\partial_\theta G_T(\theta^*)-H=O_P(T^{-1/2})\) uniformly. Together with \(D_2\rho/\varepsilon<h_-/4\), these bounds imply that, with probability tending uniformly to one, there is a unique empirical root in the closed \(\rho\)-ball about \(\theta^*\), it is \(O_P(T^{-1/2})\) from \(\theta^*\), and it is the unique member of \(\mathcal Z_T\). Hence \(\sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_T}P(E_T^c)\to0\), and
\[
 \sqrt T(\widehat\theta_T-\theta^*)+H^{-1}T^{-1/2}S_T=O_P(e_T)
\]
uniformly.

For every basin \(j\in\mathcal J\), the basin-conditional Gaussian approximation is uniform:
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_T}\sup_{\|c\|_2=1}\sup_{z\in\mathbb R}
 \left|P\!\left\{c^\top\sqrt T(\widehat\theta_T-\theta^*)\le z\mid J=j\right\}
 -\Phi\!\left(\frac{z}{\sqrt{c^\top V_jc}}\right)\right|
 \longrightarrow0.
\]
More strongly, the corresponding joint \(\sigma(J)\)-stable Gaussian kernel is expressed by
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_T}\sup_{\|c\|_2=1}\sup_{z\in\mathbb R}
 \sup_{\psi:\{1,\ldots,m\}\to[-1,1]}
 \left|E_P\!\left[\psi(J)\mathbf1\!\left\{
 c^\top\sqrt T(\widehat\theta_T-\theta^*)\le z\right\}\right]
 -\sum_{j=1}^mp_j\psi(j)\Phi\!\left(\frac{z}{\sqrt{c^\top V_jc}}\right)\right|
 \longrightarrow0.
\]
Moreover,
\[
 \frac{\omega_-}{(KD_1)^2}I_d\preceq V_j
 \preceq\frac{KB^2}{\varepsilon h_-^2}I_d
 \quad\text{for every }j\in\mathcal J.
\]
Thus, for every sequence \(P_T\in\mathfrak P_T\), the laws of \(V_J\) have a weakly convergent subsequence with a limiting law \(\mu\) supported on the displayed compact covariance set. Along that subsequence, every fixed nonzero contrast has the centered Gaussian scale-mixture limit \(\sqrt{c^\top Vc}\,Z_1\), where \(V\sim\mu\), \(Z_1\sim N(0,1)\), and \(V\) and \(Z_1\) are independent. This limit is Gaussian if and only if \(c^\top Vc\) is \(\mu\)-almost surely constant. No pointwise convergence of \(\eta_t\) is used.
statements.justification: This theorem derives predictable-QV control, exact-root localization, basin-conditional Gaussian limits, and the joint sigma(J)-stable Gaussian kernel from separated finite attractors and one common Cesaro modulus.

Write \(g_{t,a}(\theta)=g(a,X_t,Y_t(a);\theta)\). By sequential randomization, conditional independence of \(A_t\) and the current potential outcomes, the independent full-data arrival assumption, and overlap,
\[
\begin{aligned}
 E_P[\xi_t\mid\mathcal F_{t-1}]
 &=E_P\!\left[E_P\!\left\{\left.\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}
 \frac{\mathbf1\{A_t=a\}g_{t,a}(\theta^*)}
 {\pi_t(a\mid X_t,\mathcal F_{t-1})}\right|W_t,\mathcal F_{t-1}\right\}\middle|\mathcal F_{t-1}\right]\\
 &=E_P\!\left[\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}g_{t,a}(\theta^*)\right]
 =M_P(\theta^*)=0.
\end{aligned}
\tag{1}
\]
Thus \((\xi_t,\mathcal F_t)\) is a martingale-difference array. The same conditioning calculation and \(\mathrm{def:basin\text{-}covariance}\) give
\[
 E_P[\xi_t\xi_t^\top\mid\mathcal F_{t-1}]=\Gamma_P(\eta_{t-1}),
 \qquad \Omega_J=\Gamma_P(\bar\eta_J).
\tag{2}
\]
The bounded-score and overlap assumptions imply \(\|\xi_t\|_2\le B/\varepsilon\). For every unit vector \(u\),
\[
 u^\top\Gamma_P(\eta)u
 \le E_P\!\left[\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}
 \frac{\|g_{t,a}(\theta^*)\|_2^2}{\Pi(a\mid X_t,\eta)}\right]
 \le\frac{KB^2}{\varepsilon}.
\tag{3}
\]
Consequently \(\Omega_j\preceq(KB^2/\varepsilon)I_d\). Because every event \(\{J=j\}\) has probability at least \(p_->0\), the assumption \(\Omega_\infty=\Omega_J\succeq\omega_-I_d\) almost surely implies \(\Omega_j\succeq\omega_-I_d\) for every \(j\). Differentiation through the finite sum and expectation is justified by the common derivative envelope, and hence
\[
 \|H\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le E_P\!\left[\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}
 \|\partial_\theta g_{t,a}(\theta^*)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\right]
 \le KD_1.
\tag{4}
\]

For \(p,q\ge\varepsilon\), \(|p^{-1}-q^{-1}|\le|p-q|/\varepsilon^2\). The policy Lipschitz condition and the definition of \(\Gamma_P\) therefore yield
\[
 \|\Gamma_P(\eta)-\Gamma_P(\eta')\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le L_\Gamma\|\eta-\eta'\|_2,
 \qquad L_\Gamma=\frac{KB^2L_\Pi}{\varepsilon^2},
\tag{5}
\]
and \(\|\Gamma_P(\eta)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le M_\Gamma:=KB^2/\varepsilon\). On
\[
 \mathcal A_T=\left\{T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^T
 \|\eta_{t-1}-\bar\eta_J\|_2\le r_T\right\},
\]
equations (2) and (5) imply
\[
 \left\|T^{-1}\langle S\rangle_T-\Omega_J\right\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le L_\Gamma r_T.
\tag{6}
\]
On \(\mathcal A_T^c\) the norm is at most \(2M_\Gamma\), and the uniform attraction assumption gives \(P(\mathcal A_T^c)\le\delta_T\). Thus
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_T}E_P\left\|T^{-1}\langle S\rangle_T-\Omega_J\right\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le L_\Gamma r_T+2M_\Gamma\delta_T
 \le C(r_T+\delta_T).
\tag{7}
\]

We next establish the exact-root expansion. For fixed \(\theta\), sequential randomization and independent full-data arrivals make the summands of \(G_T(\theta)-M_P(\theta)\) mean-zero martingale differences. Their norms are uniformly bounded, so martingale orthogonality gives
\[
 E_P\|G_T(\theta)-M_P(\theta)\|_2^2\le C_0/T.
\tag{8}
\]
The empirical and population maps are uniformly Lipschitz in \(\theta\), with respective moduli \(D_1/\varepsilon\) and \(KD_1\). A finite mesh of the fixed compact set \(\Theta\), Chebyshev's inequality applied to (8), and a union bound therefore show, for every fixed \(x>0\),
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_T}P\left\{\sup_{\theta\in\Theta}
 \|G_T(\theta)-M_P(\theta)\|_2>x\right\}\longrightarrow0.
\tag{9}
\]
Since \(M_P(\theta^*)=0\) and the preliminary estimator satisfies its defining approximate-minimum inequality,
\[
 \|M_P(\widetilde\theta_T)\|_2
 \le2\sup_{\theta\in\Theta}\|G_T(\theta)-M_P(\theta)\|_2
 +T^{-1/2}(r_T+\delta_T)=o_P(1)
\tag{10}
\]
uniformly. Root separation then implies, for every \(u>0\),
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_T}P\{\|\widetilde\theta_T-\theta^*\|_2\ge u\}
 \le\sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_T}P\{\|M_P(\widetilde\theta_T)\|_2\ge\kappa(u)\}
 \longrightarrow0.
\tag{11}
\]

At \(\theta^*\), \(G_T(\theta^*)=S_T/T\). Equations (1) and (3), martingale orthogonality, and fixed \(d\) give \(G_T(\theta^*)=O_P(T^{-1/2})\) uniformly. The identical entrywise argument for the bounded derivative score gives
\[
 R_T:=\partial_\theta G_T(\theta^*)-H=O_P(T^{-1/2})
\tag{12}
\]
uniformly. On the closed \(\rho\)-ball about \(\theta^*\), the curvature and overlap assumptions imply
\[
 \sup_{\|\theta-\theta^*\|_2\le\rho}
 \|\partial_\theta G_T(\theta)-H\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le\|R_T\|_{\mathrm{op}}+D_2\rho/\varepsilon.
\tag{13}
\]
The radius restriction, (12), and \(\sigma_{\min}(H)\ge h_-\) make the right-hand side less than \(h_-/2\) with probability tending uniformly to one. On that event define \(\Psi_T(\theta)=\theta-H^{-1}G_T(\theta)\). Since \(\|H^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le h_-^{-1}\), equation (13) makes \(\Psi_T\) a contraction with modulus at most \(1/2\), and
\[
 \|\Psi_T(\theta)-\theta^*\|_2
 \le\tfrac12\|\theta-\theta^*\|_2+h_-^{-1}\|G_T(\theta^*)\|_2.
\tag{14}
\]
With probability tending uniformly to one, the last term is at most \(\rho/2\), and root interiority puts the entire closed ball in \(\Theta\). Starting from \(\theta^*\), iterate \(\theta^{(n+1)}=\Psi_T(\theta^{(n)})\). Equation (14) keeps every iterate in the closed ball, and the contraction bound gives \(\|\theta^{(n+1)}-\theta^{(n)}\|_2\le2^{-n}\|\theta^{(1)}-\theta^{(0)}\|_2\). The geometric-series bound makes the iterates Cauchy; completeness of \(\mathbb R^d\), closedness of the ball, and continuity of \(\Psi_T\) give a fixed point \(\theta_T^0\). If two fixed points existed, the contraction inequality would make their distance at most half itself, so the fixed point is unique. Since a fixed point of \(\Psi_T\) is a zero of \(G_T\),
\[
 \|\theta_T^0-\theta^*\|_2
 \le2h_-^{-1}\|G_T(\theta^*)\|_2=O_P(T^{-1/2}).
\tag{15}
\]
Equations (11) and (15) put both \(\widetilde\theta_T\) and \(\theta_T^0\) within \(\rho/4\) of \(\theta^*\) with probability tending uniformly to one. Then \(\theta_T^0\in\mathcal Z_T\), while every member of \(\mathcal Z_T\) is within \(3\rho/4\) of \(\theta^*\) and therefore equals \(\theta_T^0\). Hence \(\sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_T}P(E_T^c)\to0\), and the selected estimator equals \(\theta_T^0\) outside a uniformly negligible event.

Put \(\Delta_T=\widehat\theta_T-\theta^*\). On the exact-root event, Taylor's formula and the curvature envelope give
\[
 0=T^{-1}S_T+H\Delta_T+R_T\Delta_T+R_T^{(2)},
 \qquad \|R_T^{(2)}\|_2\le\frac{D_2}{2\varepsilon}\|\Delta_T\|_2^2.
\tag{16}
\]
Using (12), (15), and \(\|H^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le h_-^{-1}\) in (16) yields
\[
 \sqrt T\Delta_T+H^{-1}T^{-1/2}S_T
 =O_P(T^{-1/2})=O_P(e_T).
\tag{17}
\]
The fallback event is uniformly negligible, so (17) holds unconditionally in the uniform-in-probability sense.

It remains to prove the basin-stable law. Let
\[
 \beta_T=\max\{T^{-1/2},\sqrt{r_T}\},
 \qquad k_T=\lceil T\beta_T\rceil.
\tag{18}
\]
For all sufficiently large \(T\), \(1\le k_T<T\), while the vanishing-modulus condition gives
\[
 \frac{k_T}{T}\longrightarrow0,
 \qquad \frac{Tr_T}{k_T}\le\frac{r_T}{\beta_T}\le\sqrt{r_T}\longrightarrow0.
\tag{19}
\]
Define the prefix average \(\bar\eta_T^{\mathrm{pre}}=k_T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^{k_T}\eta_{t-1}\), and let \(J_T\) be its nearest member of \(\{\bar\eta_1,\ldots,\bar\eta_m\}\), with deterministic tie-breaking. Then \(J_T\) is \(\mathcal F_{k_T}\)-measurable. On \(\mathcal A_T\),
\[
 \|\bar\eta_T^{\mathrm{pre}}-\bar\eta_J\|_2
 \le\frac{Tr_T}{k_T}.
\tag{20}
\]
If \(m=1\), then \(J_T=J=1\) identically. If \(m\ge2\), (19) makes the right-hand side eventually less than \(s_\eta/2\), and the separation condition then makes \(\bar\eta_J\) the unique nearest attractor. In either case,
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_T}P(J_T\ne J)\le\delta_T\longrightarrow0.
\tag{21}
\]
Since \(P(J=j)\ge p_-\), equation (21) also gives \(P(J_T=j)\ge p_-/2\) for every \(j\) and all sufficiently large \(T\), uniformly in \(P\).

Fix a unit vector \(c\), put \(a=H^{-\top}c\), and define \(X_t=-a^\top\xi_t\). Equations (3)--(4) and Jacobian nonsingularity imply
\[
 \frac1{KD_1}\le\|a\|_2\le\frac1{h_-},
 \qquad |X_t|\le L:=\frac{B}{\varepsilon h_-},
\tag{22}
\]
and, for \(\lambda_j=a^\top\Omega_ja=c^\top V_jc\),
\[
 v_0:=\frac{\omega_-}{(KD_1)^2}\le\lambda_j
 \le v_1:=\frac{KB^2}{\varepsilon h_-^2}.
\tag{23}
\]
On \(\mathcal A_T\cap\{J=j\}\), equations (5) and (19) give
\[
 \left\|T^{-1}\sum_{t=k_T+1}^T\Gamma_P(\eta_{t-1})-\Omega_j\right\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le L_\Gamma r_T+M_\Gamma k_T/T.
\tag{24}
\]
The left-hand side is always at most \(2M_\Gamma\). Conditioning (24) on \(J_T=j\), using \(P(J_T=j)\ge p_-/2\), and charging \(\mathcal A_T^c\) and \(\{J_T\ne J\}\) to (21), yields
\[
 E_P\!\left[\left.\left|T^{-1}\sum_{t=k_T+1}^T
 E_P[X_t^2\mid\mathcal F_{t-1}]-\lambda_j\right|\ \right|J_T=j\right]
 \le C\{r_T+k_T/T+\delta_T\}\longrightarrow0
\tag{25}
\]
uniformly in \(P,c,j\).

Because \(\{J_T=j\}\in\mathcal F_{k_T}\), the suffix \((X_t,\mathcal F_t)_{t=k_T+1}^T\) remains a martingale-difference array under the conditional law \(P(\,\cdot\mid J_T=j)\): for \(t>k_T\), multiplication by the \(\mathcal F_{t-1}\)-measurable indicator \(\mathbf1\{J_T=j\}\) preserves the zero conditional mean in (1). Apply \(\mathrm{lem:early\text{-}measurable\text{-}martingale\text{-}mixture}\) under that conditional law with early time \(k_T\), constant \(\lambda_T=\lambda_j\), increment bound \(L\), and the common lower and upper bounds in (23). Equation (25) verifies its predictable-variation premise. Hence
\[
 \sup_{P,c,j,z}\left|P\!\left\{T^{-1/2}\sum_{t=k_T+1}^TX_t\le z\mid J_T=j\right\}
 -\Phi\!\left(\frac z{\sqrt{\lambda_j}}\right)\right|\longrightarrow0.
\tag{26}
\]
Here and below the displayed supremum ranges over \(P\in\mathfrak P_T\), unit \(c\), \(1\le j\le m\), and \(z\in\mathbb R\), as applicable.

Martingale orthogonality, (22), and the basin-mass floor give
\[
 E_P\!\left[\left.\left|T^{-1/2}\sum_{t=1}^{k_T}X_t\right|^2\right|J_T=j\right]
 \le \frac{2L^2k_T}{p_-T}=o(1).
\tag{27}
\]
Indeed the numerator restricted to \(\{J_T=j\}\) is at most the unconditional second moment, which equals the sum of the increment second moments by martingale orthogonality. The same argument applies conditionally on \(J=j\), with denominator at least \(p_-\). The remainder in (17) is uniformly \(o_P(1)\), and conditioning preserves that conclusion because \(P(J=j)\ge p_-\). To transfer (26), if \(Y\) denotes the suffix sum and \(R\) the sum of the prefix and linearization remainders, then for every \(h>0\),
\[
 P(Y\le z-h)-P(|R|>h)\le P(Y+R\le z)
 \le P(Y\le z+h)+P(|R|>h).
\]
The Gaussian laws in (26) have densities bounded uniformly by \((2\pi v_0)^{-1/2}\). First choose \(h\) small and then use (27) and the conditional \(o_P(1)\) remainder to make \(P(|R|>h)\) uniformly small. This proves the required transfer. Finally, for every event \(B\),
\[
 \left|P(B\mid J=j)-P(B\mid J_T=j)\right|
 \le \frac{2P(J_T\ne J)}{\min\{P(J=j),P(J_T=j)\}}
 \le\frac{4\delta_T}{p_-}.
\tag{28}
\]
Equations (21), (26)--(28), and \(\lambda_j=c^\top V_jc\) prove the displayed basin-conditional approximation.

For any \(\psi:\{1,\ldots,m\}\to[-1,1]\), decompose by the disjoint events \(\{J=j\}\):
\[
 E_P[\psi(J)\mathbf1\{Z_T\le z\}]
 =\sum_{j=1}^mp_j\psi(j)P(Z_T\le z\mid J=j),
 \qquad Z_T=c^\top\sqrt T(\widehat\theta_T-\theta^*).
\tag{29}
\]
The absolute difference between (29) and the asserted Gaussian-kernel sum is at most the maximum conditional Kolmogorov error, because \(\sum_jp_j|\psi(j)|\le1\). This proves the joint \(\sigma(J)\)-stable formula uniformly over \(\psi\). Equation (23) for every unit \(c\) is equivalent to the asserted Loewner bounds on every \(V_j\). Equation (2), the terminal-selection assumption, and the covariance definition give \(\Omega_\infty=\Omega_J\) and \(V_\infty=V_J\).

The compact covariance subsequence lemma now supplies a weakly convergent subsequence of the laws of \(V_J\). Along it, the marginal case \(\psi\equiv1\), continuity of \(v\mapsto\Phi(z/\sqrt{c^\top vc})\) on the compact covariance set, and the preceding uniform approximation give the limit law \(\sqrt{c^\top Vc}\,Z_1\). If \(c^\top Vc=q_0\) almost surely, this is \(N(0,q_0)\). Conversely, if it is \(N(0,\sigma^2)\), compact support permits comparison of second and fourth moments. For the standard normal density \(\phi\), integration by parts using \(\phi'(z)=-z\phi(z)\) gives \(E[Z_1^2]=1\) and \(E[Z_1^4]=3\). Independence therefore gives
\[
 E[c^\top Vc]=\sigma^2,
 \qquad 3E[(c^\top Vc)^2]=3\sigma^4,
\]
so \(\operatorname{Var}(c^\top Vc)=0\). Thus the mixture is Gaussian exactly when its projected scale is constant. The early proxy \(J_T\) was constructed solely from the common Cesaro attraction event; no pointwise convergence of the policy state was used.

Using the exact-root linearization on \(E_T\) and carrying its uniformly negligible fallback event \(E_T^c\), uniformly over \(P\in\mathfrak P_T\),
\[
 T^{-1}([S]_T-\langle S\rangle_T)=O_P(T^{-1/2}),\qquad
 \widehat\Omega_T-\Omega_\infty=O_P(e_T),\qquad
 \widehat H_T-H=O_P(e_T).
\]
Consequently \(\sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_T}P(\mathcal E_T^c)\to0\), the event truncation is asymptotically inactive uniformly, and \(\widehat V_T-V_\infty=O_P(e_T)\). Moreover,
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_T}\sup_{\|c\|_2=1}\sup_{z\in\mathbb R}
 \left|P\{T_T^{\mathrm{rqv}}(c)\le z\}-\Phi(z)\right|\longrightarrow0.
\]
For the realized-QV interval \(I_T^{\mathrm{rqv}}(c,\alpha)\) in \(\mathrm{def:realized\text{-}qv\text{-}wald\text{-}interval}\), every fixed \(\alpha\in(0,1)\) satisfies
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_T}\sup_{\|c\|_2=1}
 \left|P\{\tau\in I_T^{\mathrm{rqv}}(c,\alpha)\}-(1-\alpha)\right|\longrightarrow0.
\]
This derives the self-normalized variance-ratio, invertibility-event, and inverse-QV controls from the terminal-representative Cesaro attraction and exact-root localization primitives. The class and estimator are neither a subclass nor a superclass of Saco's published pointwise AIPW/DML setup as stated.
statements.justification: The always-defined truncated sandwich tracks the arbitrary terminal covariance, becomes asymptotically untruncated uniformly, and removes even a continuously mixed Gaussian scale without estimating its mixing law.
statements.gap: Saco proves a pointwise self-normalized result for a distinct AIPW/DML setup. This theorem verifies variance growth, realized-to-predictable QV, exact-root, feasible-inverse, and truncation controls uniformly for the present bounded IPW-Z terminal-representative class; neither published class contains the other as stated.
statements.consumer: The theorem gives a feasible standard-normal Wald interval for HeartSteps-style causal excursion contrasts under path-dependent adaptive assignment.
statements.proof_tex:
All stochastic orders are uniform over \(P\in\mathfrak P_T\) and, where present, unit contrasts. Bounded scores and overlap give
\[
 \|\xi_t\|_2\le M_\xi:=B/\varepsilon.
\tag{1}
\]
Define \(D_t=\xi_t\xi_t^\top-E_P[\xi_t\xi_t^\top\mid\mathcal F_{t-1}]\). Every entry of \(D_t\) is a martingale difference and \(\|D_t\|_{\mathrm F}\le2M_\xi^2\). Orthogonality over the fixed \(d^2\) entries yields
\[
 E_P\left\|T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^TD_t\right\|_{\mathrm F}^2
 =T^{-2}\sum_{t=1}^TE_P\|D_t\|_{\mathrm F}^2
 \le\frac{4M_\xi^4}{T}.
\tag{2}
\]
Since operator norm is bounded by Frobenius norm, Chebyshev's inequality gives
\[
 T^{-1}([S]_T-\langle S\rangle_T)=O_P(T^{-1/2}).
\tag{3}
\]

Theorem \(\mathrm{thm:basin\text{-}stable\text{-}ipwz}\) gives
\[
 \|\widehat\theta_T-\theta^*\|_2=O_P(T^{-1/2}),
 \qquad \partial_\theta G_T(\theta^*)-H=O_P(T^{-1/2}).
\tag{4}
\]
For every \(t\), the derivative and overlap bounds imply
\[
 \|\widehat\xi_t-\xi_t\|_2
 \le\frac{D_1}{\varepsilon}\|\widehat\theta_T-\theta^*\|_2.
\tag{5}
\]
Both scores have norm at most \(M_\xi\), so
\[
 \|\widehat\xi_t\widehat\xi_t^\top-\xi_t\xi_t^\top\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le\frac{2BD_1}{\varepsilon^2}\|\widehat\theta_T-\theta^*\|_2.
\tag{6}
\]
Averaging (6), then using (3)--(4), the predictable-QV expectation bound in Theorem \(\mathrm{thm:basin\text{-}stable\text{-}ipwz}\), and Markov's inequality, gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \|\widehat\Omega_T-\Omega_J\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 &\le\left\|T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^T
 (\widehat\xi_t\widehat\xi_t^\top-\xi_t\xi_t^\top)\right\|_{\mathrm{op}}\\
 &\quad+\left\|T^{-1}([S]_T-\langle S\rangle_T)\right\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 +\left\|T^{-1}\langle S\rangle_T-\Omega_J\right\|_{\mathrm{op}}\\
 &=O_P(T^{-1/2}+r_T+\delta_T)=O_P(e_T).
\end{aligned}
\tag{7}
\]
On the closed \(\rho\)-ball, curvature and overlap similarly imply, outside the negligible fallback event,
\[
 \|\widehat H_T-H\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le\|\partial_\theta G_T(\theta^*)-H\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 +\frac{D_2}{\varepsilon}\|\widehat\theta_T-\theta^*\|_2
 =O_P(T^{-1/2})=O_P(e_T).
\tag{8}
\]
The fallback probability tends uniformly to zero, so (8) holds unconditionally in the uniform-in-probability sense.

The variational definitions give \(|\sigma_{\min}(A)-\sigma_{\min}(B)|\le\|A-B\|_{\mathrm{op}}\) and, for symmetric matrices, \(|\lambda_{\min}(A)-\lambda_{\min}(B)|\le\|A-B\|_{\mathrm{op}}\). Thus (7)--(8), \(\sigma_{\min}(H)\ge h_-\), and \(\Omega_J\succeq\omega_-I_d\) imply
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_T}P(\mathcal E_T^c)\longrightarrow0.
\tag{9}
\]
On \(\mathcal E_T\), every inverse is legally evaluated and
\[
 \widehat H_T^{-1}-H^{-1}
 =\widehat H_T^{-1}(H-\widehat H_T)H^{-1},
 \qquad \|\widehat H_T^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le2/h_-.
\tag{10}
\]
Theorem \(\mathrm{thm:basin\text{-}stable\text{-}ipwz}\) also gives \(\|H^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le h_-^{-1}\) and \(\|\Omega_J\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le KB^2/\varepsilon\). Inserting and subtracting the three sandwich factors one at a time and using (7)--(10) proves on \(\mathcal E_T\) that
\[
 \widehat H_T^{-1}\widehat\Omega_T\widehat H_T^{-\top}
 -H^{-1}\Omega_JH^{-\top}=O_P(e_T).
\tag{11}
\]
On \(\mathcal E_T^c\), \(\widehat V_T=I_d\), while Theorem \(\mathrm{thm:basin\text{-}stable\text{-}ipwz}\) bounds \(V_J\) uniformly. Equation (9) makes this branch negligible, so
\[
 \widehat V_T-V_J=O_P(e_T).
\tag{12}
\]

Fix a unit vector \(c\), and define
\[
 a=H^{-\top}c,\quad U_t=a^\top\xi_t,\quad
 A_T^2=\sum_{t=1}^TE_P[U_t^2\mid\mathcal F_{t-1}],\quad
 Q_T=\sum_{t=1}^TU_t^2.
\tag{13}
\]
The Jacobian bounds from Theorem \(\mathrm{thm:basin\text{-}stable\text{-}ipwz}\) give
\[
 (KD_1)^{-1}\le\|a\|_2\le h_-^{-1},
 \qquad |U_t|\le L:=\frac{B}{\varepsilon h_-}.
\tag{14}
\]
The predictable-QV approximation and basin nondegeneracy imply
\[
 \frac{A_T^2}{T}
 =a^\top(T^{-1}\langle S\rangle_T)a
 =a^\top\Omega_Ja+o_P(1),
 \qquad a^\top\Omega_Ja\ge v_0:=\frac{\omega_-}{(KD_1)^2}>0.
\tag{15}
\]
Thus \(A_T^2\to\infty\) in probability uniformly. Equation (3) gives
\[
 \frac{Q_T-A_T^2}{T}
 =a^\top T^{-1}([S]_T-\langle S\rangle_T)a
 =O_P(T^{-1/2}),
\tag{16}
\]
so \(Q_T/A_T^2\to_P1\) and \(P(Q_T>0)\to1\) uniformly. With \(\delta=2\), (14)--(15) imply
\[
 A_T^{-4}\sum_{t=1}^TE_P|U_t|^4
 \le A_T^{-4}TL^4\longrightarrow_P0.
\tag{17}
\]
Indeed, on \(A_T^2/T\ge v_0/2\), the right-hand side is at most \(4L^4/(Tv_0^2)\), and that event has probability tending uniformly to one.

Every array formed by an arbitrary sequence \(P_T\in\mathfrak P_T\) and unit contrasts \(c_T\) satisfies the hypotheses of \(\mathrm{lem:saco\text{-}self\text{-}normalized\text{-}martingale\text{-}clt}\). Hence
\[
 \frac{a^\top S_T}{\sqrt{a^\top[S]_Ta}}
 =\frac{\sum_{t=1}^TU_t}{\sqrt{Q_T}}\Rightarrow N(0,1).
\tag{18}
\]
This convergence is uniform: otherwise a sequence \((P_T,c_T)\) with Kolmogorov distance bounded away from zero would contradict (18) for that triangular array. Weak convergence to the continuous distribution function \(\Phi\) implies Kolmogorov convergence by a finite continuity-point partition and monotonicity.

Theorem \(\mathrm{thm:basin\text{-}stable\text{-}ipwz}\) gives
\[
 \sqrt T\,c^\top(\widehat\theta_T-\theta^*)
 =-T^{-1/2}a^\top S_T+O_P(e_T).
\tag{19}
\]
Equations (3), (7), (12), and \(c^\top V_Jc=a^\top\Omega_Ja\) imply
\[
 c^\top\widehat V_Tc-T^{-1}a^\top[S]_Ta=O_P(e_T).
\tag{20}
\]
By (15)--(16), both quantities in (20) are at least \(v_0/2\) with probability tending uniformly to one, so all divisions and square roots are legitimate on that event. Since \(e_T\to0\) and \(|\sqrt x-\sqrt y|=|x-y|/(\sqrt x+\sqrt y)\), equations (18)--(20) yield
\[
 T_T^{\mathrm{rqv}}(c)
 =-\frac{a^\top S_T}{\sqrt{a^\top[S]_Ta}}+o_P(1)
\tag{21}
\]
uniformly. Explicitly, for every \(h>0\), applying
\[
 P(Y\le z-h)-P(|R|>h)\le P(Y+R\le z)
 \le P(Y\le z+h)+P(|R|>h)
\]
to the self-normalized term \(Y\) and the \(o_P(1)\) remainder \(R\), then using uniform continuity of \(\Phi\), transfers (18) to (21). Symmetry of the standard normal law removes the leading minus sign and proves the asserted uniform standard-normal approximation.

Finally, \(\tau=c^\top\theta^*\) and \(\mathrm{def:realized\text{-}qv\text{-}wald\text{-}interval}\) give
\[
 \{\tau\in I_T^{\mathrm{rqv}}(c,\alpha)\}
 =\{|T_T^{\mathrm{rqv}}(c)|\le z_{1-\alpha/2}\}.
\tag{22}
\]
The pivotal approximation and \(2\Phi(z_{1-\alpha/2})-1=1-\alpha\) give the stated uniform coverage for every fixed \(\alpha\). The cited self-normalized theorem supplies only the scalar martingale implication in (18); equations (1)--(17) verify its hypotheses from the finite-attractor IPW-Z primitives, including variance growth, realized-to-predictable quadratic variation, exact-root localization, feasible inversion, and truncation inactivity.

statements.statement:
Let \(T_\ell\to\infty\) and \(P_\ell\in\mathfrak P_{T_\ell}\) be a sequence along which the law of \(V_\infty\) under \(P_\ell\) converges weakly to a probability law \(\mu\) on the compact covariance set in Theorem 1. Let \(V\sim\mu\). Fix nonzero \(c\) and deterministic positive-definite \(\Sigma\). Then
\[
 \lim_{\ell\to\infty}P_\ell\{\tau\in C_{T_\ell}^{\Sigma}(c,\alpha)\}=1-\alpha
 \quad\text{for every }\alpha\in(0,1)
\]
if and only if
\[
 c^\top Vc=c^\top\Sigma c\qquad\mu\text{-almost surely}.
\]
The necessity identifies the projected variance law of a general centered Gaussian scale mixture from coverage at every nominal level; it makes no claim from validity at only one level.
statements.justification: This theorem exactly characterizes every-level fixed-sandwich validity for one causal contrast under an arbitrary limiting covariance mixing law.
statements.gap: Directional-stability work gives sufficient target-specific conditions and Saco highlights random predictable variance; neither gives the general scale-mixture every-level converse.
statements.consumer: Trial analysts can decide whether a deterministic variance report remains valid for one prespecified HeartSteps excursion-effect contrast even when other covariance directions remain random.
statements.proof_tex:
Set \(s=c^\top\Sigma c>0\) and \(q(v)=c^\top vc\). Positive definiteness of \(\Sigma\), the compact covariance lower bound in \(\mathrm{thm:basin\text{-}stable\text{-}ipwz}\), and \(c\ne0\) justify every square root and division below. The deterministic interval definition gives
\[
 \{\tau\in C_{T_\ell}^{\Sigma}(c,\alpha)\}
 =\left\{\left|\sqrt{T_\ell}\,c^\top(\widehat\theta_{T_\ell}-\theta^*)\right|
 \le z_{1-\alpha/2}\sqrt s\right\}.
\tag{1}
\]
For nonunit \(c\), apply \(\mathrm{thm:basin\text{-}stable\text{-}ipwz}\) to \(c/\|c\|_2\) and rescale. Taking \(\psi\equiv1\) in its stable formula gives, for every fixed \(z>0\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
 &P_\ell\!\left\{\left|\sqrt{T_\ell}\,c^\top
 (\widehat\theta_{T_\ell}-\theta^*)\right|\le z\sqrt s\right\}\\
 &\quad=E_{P_\ell}\!\left[2\Phi\!\left(z\sqrt{\frac{s}{c^\top V_Jc}}\right)-1\right]+o(1).
\end{aligned}
\tag{2}
\]
The map \(v\mapsto2\Phi(z\sqrt{s/q(v)})-1\) is bounded and continuous on the compact covariance set. Weak convergence of the laws of \(V_J\) therefore turns (2) into
\[
 \int\left\{2\Phi\!\left(z\sqrt{\frac{s}{q(v)}}\right)-1\right\}\,d\mu(v).
\tag{3}
\]
If \(q(V)=s\) \(\mu\)-almost surely, (3) equals \(2\Phi(z)-1\). Taking \(z=z_{1-\alpha/2}\) proves sufficiency at every nominal level.

Conversely, suppose the coverage limit is \(1-\alpha\) for every \(\alpha\in(0,1)\). As \(\alpha\) ranges over \((0,1)\), \(z_{1-\alpha/2}\) ranges over \((0,\infty)\). Equations (1)--(3) imply
\[
 \int\left\{2\Phi\!\left(z\sqrt{\frac{s}{q(v)}}\right)-1\right\}\,d\mu(v)
 =2\Phi(z)-1\qquad(z>0).
\tag{4}
\]
Let \(Q=q(V)\), let \(Z_1\sim N(0,1)\) be independent of \(V\), and put \(X=\sqrt QZ_1\). Both \(X/\sqrt s\) and \(Z_1\) have continuous symmetric laws. Equation (4) equates their absolute-value distribution functions at every positive argument, so symmetry gives equality of their full distributions. The compact covariance bounds make \(Q\) bounded, and equality of laws therefore permits comparison of second and fourth moments. Integration by parts for the standard normal density, using \(\phi'(z)=-z\phi(z)\), gives \(E[Z_1^2]=1\) and \(E[Z_1^4]=3\), so
\[
 E[X^2]=E[Q]=s,
 \qquad E[X^4]=3E[Q^2]=3s^2.
\tag{5}
\]
Consequently
\[
 E[(Q-s)^2]=E[Q^2]-2sE[Q]+s^2=0.
\tag{6}
\]
Thus \(Q=s\) \(\mu\)-almost surely, proving necessity. Every nominal level is essential because it supplies (4) for every \(z>0\); no conclusion was drawn from a single coverage equality.

statements.statement:
Along any sequence for which the law of \(V_\infty\) converges weakly to \(\mu\), as in Theorem 3, one deterministic positive-definite matrix \(\Sigma\) gives asymptotic coverage \(1-\alpha\) for every \(\alpha\in(0,1)\) and every nonzero contrast \(c\in\mathbb R^d\) if and only if
\[
 V=\Sigma\qquad\mu\text{-almost surely},
\]
where \(V\sim\mu\). Equivalently, the limiting covariance law is the point mass at \(\Sigma\). For a fixed law and horizon-asymptotic sequence, this specializes to \(V_\infty=\Sigma\) almost surely whenever the law of \(V_\infty\) itself is constant across horizons. The implication from all projected equalities to matrix equality uses only finitely many coordinate and pairwise-sum contrasts.
statements.justification: This theorem separates target-specific validity from target-agnostic covariance invariance for an arbitrary limiting covariance law.
statements.gap: Shen and coauthors distinguish directional from matrix stability on the sufficiency side; the general every-level necessity and finite-contrast polarization certificate remain unstated.
statements.consumer: Software reporting many adaptive-experiment contrasts can determine whether one fixed covariance matrix is defensible.
statements.proof_tex:
Suppose first that one deterministic positive-definite \(\Sigma\) gives the asserted coverage for every nonzero \(c\) and every nominal level. Apply \(\mathrm{thm:contrastwise\text{-}deterministic\text{-}sandwich\text{-}iff}\) to each of the finitely many contrasts
\[
 \mathcal C_0=\{e_r:1\le r\le d\}\cup
 \{e_r+e_s:1\le r<s\le d\}.
\tag{1}
\]
For every \(c\in\mathcal C_0\),
\[
 c^\top(V-\Sigma)c=0\qquad\mu\text{-almost surely}.
\tag{2}
\]
Because \(\mathcal C_0\) is finite, the intersection of the probability-one events in (2) still has probability one. On that intersection put \(A=V-\Sigma\), which is symmetric. Taking \(c=e_r\) gives \(A_{rr}=0\). For \(r<s\), taking \(c=e_r+e_s\) and using the diagonal equalities gives
\[
 0=(e_r+e_s)^\top A(e_r+e_s)=2A_{rs}.
\tag{3}
\]
Every entry of \(A\) vanishes, so \(V=\Sigma\) \(\mu\)-almost surely.

Conversely, if \(V=\Sigma\) \(\mu\)-almost surely, then \(c^\top Vc=c^\top\Sigma c\) almost surely for every nonzero \(c\). The contrastwise theorem gives coverage \(1-\alpha\) for every such \(c\) and every \(\alpha\in(0,1)\). This proves both directions and the point-mass formulation. If the law of \(V_\infty\) is constant across horizons along a fixed horizon-asymptotic sequence, its weak limit is that same law, so the point-mass condition is exactly \(V_\infty=\Sigma\) almost surely.

statements.statement: For every \(\varepsilon\in(0,1/6)\), the bounded witness \(P^{\dagger}\) belongs at every \(T\ge2\) to a class \(\mathfrak P_T\) with common choices \(B=2\), \(D_1=D_2=1\), \(h_-=1\), \(L_\Pi=1/12\), \(\omega_-=1\), \(\kappa(u)=u\), \(s_\Theta=1\), \(\rho=\varepsilon/8\), \(r_T=1/(2T)\), and \(\delta_T=0\). Specifically, the policy floor is \(1/6\), \(\sup_{a,\theta}\|g(a,X_t,Y_t(a);\theta)\|_2<2\), the derivative and curvature bounds are \(1\) and \(0\), \(M_{P^{\dagger}}(\theta)=-\theta\), every empirical moment admits an exact minimum of zero in \(\Theta\), and \(T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^T\|\eta_{t-1}-\bar\eta_J\|_2=1/(2T)\) almost surely. Moreover, \(P^{\dagger}(J=1)=2/5\), \(P^{\dagger}(J=2)=3/5\), so \(\mathcal J=\{1,2\}\); tail selection is exact after the first assignment, \(H=-I_2\), \(\Omega_1=V_1=\operatorname{diag}(1,2)\), and \(\Omega_2=V_2=\operatorname{diag}(1,3)\). Hence for \(\Sigma=\operatorname{diag}(1,2)\) and \(c=(1,0)^\top\), \(c^\top V_jc=c^\top\Sigma c=1\) in both positive-mass basins although \(V_1\ne V_2\), so contrastwise deterministic-sandwich validity holds while matrixwise invariance fails.
statements.justification: This elementary bounded construction verifies inside the stated law class that the contrastwise and matrixwise frontiers are logically distinct.
statements.gap: This is a non-novel existence witness, not evidence about the Guo--Xu recursion; its role is to prevent the directional and matrix claims from being conflated by an unattained free-matrix example.
statements.consumer: Applied analysts can retain a valid primary-endpoint interval in a concrete adaptive experiment without claiming that all secondary contrasts share a stable covariance.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(\varepsilon\in(0,1/6)\), \(T\ge2\), and the law \(P^{\dagger}\) in \(\mathrm{def:directional\text{-}matrix\text{-}witness}\). The context is constant, and the two nonzero potential outcomes are independent across occasions and arms with the displayed time-invariant laws. Hence the full-data vectors are independent and identically distributed. At occasion \(t\), \(\eta_{t-1}\) is \(\mathcal F_{t-1}\)-measurable and the action is drawn from \(\Pi(\cdot\mid X_t,\eta_{t-1})\) independently of current potential outcomes, verifying sequential randomization.

Writing \(u\in[0,1]\) for the state, linear interpolation gives
\[
 \Pi(1\mid x,u)=\frac25,\qquad
 \Pi(2\mid x,u)=\frac14-\frac{u}{12},\qquad
 \Pi(3\mid x,u)=\frac7{20}+\frac{u}{12}.
\tag{1}
\]
The probabilities sum to one and their coordinatewise minimum is \(1/6>\varepsilon\), proving overlap. Also
\[
 \sup_{a\in\{1,2,3\}}|\Pi(a\mid x,u)-\Pi(a\mid x,u')|
 \le\frac1{12}|u-u'|,
\tag{2}
\]
so \(L_\Pi=1/12\) is valid.

For every \(\theta\in[-1,1]^2\),
\[
 |Y_t(1)-\theta_1|\le1+\sqrt{2/5}<2,
 \qquad |Y_t(2)-\theta_2|\le1+\sqrt{1/2}<2.
\tag{3}
\]
Each nonzero score has only one nonzero coordinate and the third-arm score is zero, so \(B=2\) is a common envelope. The score is affine in \(\theta\) on \(\mathbb R^2\), with derivative matrices
\[
 \begin{pmatrix}-1&0\\0&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad
 \begin{pmatrix}0&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix},\qquad 0.
\]
Their operator norms are at most one and all second derivatives vanish. Thus \(D_1=D_2=1\) are valid envelopes, with actual curvature zero.

Both nonzero outcomes have mean zero. Therefore
\[
 M_{P^{\dagger}}(\theta)=(-\theta_1,-\theta_2)^\top=-\theta,
 \qquad H=-I_2.
\tag{4}
\]
It follows that \(\theta^*=0\) is the unique root, \(\|M_{P^{\dagger}}(\theta)\|_2=\|\theta\|_2\), and \(\sigma_{\min}(H)=1\). Hence \(\kappa(u)=u\) and \(h_-=1\) are valid, while
\[
 \operatorname{dist}(0,\partial[-1,1]^2)=1
\tag{5}
\]
gives \(s_\Theta=1\).

For completeness, the empirical moment has an exact zero for every assignment and outcome array. For \(a\in\{1,2\}\), put
\[
 W_a=\sum_{t=1}^T\frac{\mathbf1\{A_t=a\}}
 {\pi_t(a\mid X_t,\mathcal F_{t-1})}.
\]
If \(W_a>0\), define
\[
 \theta_a^{(0)}=
 \frac{\sum_{t=1}^T\mathbf1\{A_t=a\}Y_t(a)/
 \pi_t(a\mid X_t,\mathcal F_{t-1})}{W_a};
\tag{6}
\]
if \(W_a=0\), set \(\theta_a^{(0)}=0\). In the first case (6) is a convex combination of values in \([-1,1]\), and in the second case the corresponding empirical coordinate is identically zero. Hence \(\theta^{(0)}\in\Theta\), direct substitution gives \(G_T(\theta^{(0)})=0\), and
\[
 \min_{\theta\in\Theta}\|G_T(\theta)\|_2=0.
\tag{7}
\]

At the first occasion \(\eta_0=1/2\), and (1) gives \(P^{\dagger}(A_1=1)=2/5\). Since \(J=1\) exactly when \(A_1=1\),
\[
 P^{\dagger}(J=1)=\frac25,
 \qquad P^{\dagger}(J=2)=\frac35.
\tag{8}
\]
The label \(J\) is \(\mathcal F_1\)-measurable, \(\eta_\infty=\bar\eta_J\), and the two fixed attractors have distance one. Thus the finite-tail-selection assumption holds with \(m=2\), the finite-attractor-separation assumption holds with \(s_\eta=1\), and the basin-mass-floor assumption holds with \(p_-=2/5\). The construction sets \(\eta_s=\bar\eta_J\) for every \(s\ge1\), while \(|\eta_0-\bar\eta_J|=1/2\). Consequently
\[
 \frac1T\sum_{t=1}^T|\eta_{t-1}-\bar\eta_J|=\frac1{2T}
 \quad\text{almost surely}.
\tag{9}
\]
Thus the attraction condition holds with \(r_T=1/(2T)\) and \(\delta_T=0\), and
\[
 e_T=T^{-1/2}+\frac1{2T}\longrightarrow0.
\tag{10}
\]
The proposed radius obeys the required strict bound because
\[
 0<\rho=\frac\varepsilon8
 <\min\left\{1,\frac{\varepsilon h_-}{4D_2}\right\}
 =\min\left\{1,\frac\varepsilon4\right\}.
\tag{11}
\]

At \(\theta^*=0\), the score outer products are diagonal, the third-arm contribution vanishes, and
\[
 E_{P^{\dagger}}[Y_t(1)^2]=\frac25,
 \qquad E_{P^{\dagger}}[Y_t(2)^2]=\frac12.
\tag{12}
\]
Using (1), (12), and \(\mathrm{def:basin\text{-}covariance}\),
\[
 \Omega_1=\operatorname{diag}\left(\frac{2/5}{2/5},\frac{1/2}{1/4}\right)
 =\operatorname{diag}(1,2),
\tag{13}
\]
and
\[
 \Omega_2=\operatorname{diag}\left(\frac{2/5}{2/5},\frac{1/2}{1/6}\right)
 =\operatorname{diag}(1,3).
\tag{14}
\]
Both matrices dominate \(I_2\), so basin nondegeneracy holds with \(\omega_-=1\). Equations (1)--(14) verify every member condition in the finite-attractor class with constants and moduli common across horizons. Therefore \(P^{\dagger}\in\mathfrak P_T\) for every \(T\ge2\).

Finally, (4) and the sandwich definition imply
\[
 V_1=\operatorname{diag}(1,2),
 \qquad V_2=\operatorname{diag}(1,3).
\tag{15}
\]
For \(\Sigma=\operatorname{diag}(1,2)\) and \(c=(1,0)^\top\),
\[
 c^\top V_1c=c^\top V_2c=c^\top\Sigma c=1,
 \qquad V_1\ne V_2.
\tag{16}
\]
Along every horizon sequence the law of \(V_J\) is
\[
 \mu=\frac25\delta_{V_1}+\frac35\delta_{V_2}.
\tag{17}
\]
The projected equality (16) and \(\mathrm{thm:contrastwise\text{-}deterministic\text{-}sandwich\text{-}iff}\) give every-level validity for this contrast. But (8), (15), and (17) make \(V_J\) nonconstant; \(\mathrm{thm:matrixwise\text{-}deterministic\text{-}sandwich\text{-}iff}\) therefore rules out validity of one deterministic sandwich for all nonzero contrasts. This proves the separation. In particular, the claim has been checked at the smallest allowed horizon \(T=2\): equation (7) holds for every realized assignment, including assignments that omit either active arm, so no hidden root-existence exception is used.

statements.statement:
Let \(p\in[1,\infty)\), \(\gamma>0\), and let \((X_i,\mathcal G_i)_{i=1}^n\) be a scalar martingale-difference sequence with \(n\ge2\) and \(\max_i\|X_i\|_\infty\le\gamma\). Put \(s^2=\sum_{i=1}^nE[X_i^2]\), \(V^2=s^{-2}\sum_{i=1}^nE[X_i^2\mid\mathcal G_{i-1}]\), and \(D=\sup_x|P\{s^{-1}\sum_iX_i\le x\}-\Phi(x)|\). There is a constant \(C_{p,\gamma}\) such that
\[
D\le C_{p,\gamma}\left\{\frac{n\log n}{s^3}+\left(\|V^2-1\|_p^p+s^{-2p}\right)^{1/(2p+1)}\right\}.
\]

source.verbatim_statement: Theorem 1.5. Let p in [1,+infinity) and gamma in (0,+infinity). There exists a constant C_{p,gamma}>0 such that for any n>=2 and any X in M_n satisfying ||X||_infinity<=gamma, D(X)<=C_{p,gamma}[n log(n)/s^3(X)+(||V^2(X)-1||_p^p+s^{-2p}(X))^{1/(2p+1)}]. (1.6)

attestation.note: Direct transcription from arXiv:1103.5050 PDF page 4 (journal page 4). The persisted locator is inaccurate: the matching statement is Theorem 1.5, inequality (1.6), not Theorem 1.4/(1.5); attested literally so D0.5 can require the citation-carrier correction.

statements.statement:
Let \((X_{n,t},\mathcal G_{n,t})_{t=1}^{k_n}\) be a scalar martingale-difference array, \(S_n=\sum_tX_{n,t}\), \(Q_n=\sum_tX_{n,t}^2\), and \(A_n^2=\sum_tE[X_{n,t}^2\mid\mathcal G_{n,t-1}]\). If \(A_n^2\to\infty\) in probability, \(P(Q_n>0)\to1\), \(Q_n/A_n^2\to1\) in probability, and for some \(\delta>0\),
\[
 A_n^{-(2+\delta)}\sum_tE[|X_{n,t}|^{2+\delta}]\to0,
\]
then \(S_n/\sqrt{Q_n}\Rightarrow N(0,1)\).

source.verbatim_statement: Theorem A.1 (Self-normalized martingale CLT (Lyapunov form)). Let (xi_{n,t},F_{n,t}) be a martingale difference array with partial sums S_n=sum_{t=1}^{k_n} xi_{n,t}. Define V_n^2=sum E[xi_{n,t}^2|F_{n,t-1}] and Q_n=sum xi_{n,t}^2. Assume: (i) V_n^2 converges in probability to infinity; (ii) P(Q_n>0) tends to 1 and Q_n/V_n^2 converges in probability to 1; and (iii) for some delta>0, V_n^{-(2+delta)} sum E[|xi_{n,t}|^{2+delta}] tends to 0. Then S_n/sqrt(Q_n) converges in distribution to N(0,1).

upstream.citation: Hall and Heyde, Martingale Limit Theory and Its Application (1980)

attestation.note: Direct transcription from arXiv:2602.15559v1 PDF Appendix A, page 25. The paper says this statement is a direct corollary of Hall and Heyde (1980), Theorem 3.10, combined with Slutsky.

statements.statement: For Saco's logged-propensity, predictably scored martingale AIPW/DML estimator at a prespecified horizon, the realized-quadratic-variation score statistic and its feasible Studentized version converge pointwise to \(N(0,1)\), and the associated Wald interval has asymptotically correct coverage without a deterministic variance-stabilization assumption.

source.verbatim_statement: Theorem 5.14 (Studentized fixed-horizon inference without variance stabilization). Under the listed assumptions, S_T/sqrt(Q_T) converges in distribution to N(0,1), and the practical Studentized statistic sqrt(n_eff)(theta_hat-theta_0)/V_hat^{1/2} converges in distribution to N(0,1). Consequently, the Wald interval (4.7) has asymptotically correct coverage at the prespecified horizon, without requiring variance stabilization.

attestation.note: Direct transcription, with notation linearized but wording preserved, from arXiv:2602.15559v1 PDF page 15, Theorem 5.14 and equations (5.5)-(5.6).

statements.statement:
Let \((X_{T,t},\mathcal G_{T,t})_{t=1}^T\) be a scalar martingale-difference triangular array under \(P\), let \(0\le k_T<T\), and suppose \(|X_{T,t}|\le L<\infty\) almost surely. Let \(\lambda_T\) be \(\mathcal G_{T,k_T}\)-measurable and satisfy \(0<v_-\le\lambda_T\le v_+<\infty\) almost surely. If
\[
 \Delta_T:=E_P\left|T^{-1}\sum_{t=k_T+1}^T
 E_P[X_{T,t}^2\mid\mathcal G_{T,t-1}]-\lambda_T\right|\longrightarrow0,
\]
then
\[
 \sup_{z\in\mathbb R}\left|P\left\{T^{-1/2}\sum_{t=k_T+1}^T X_{T,t}\le z\right\}
 -E_P\Phi\left(\frac{z}{\sqrt{\lambda_T}}\right)\right|\longrightarrow0.
\]
The conclusion is uniform over any collection of arrays having common \(L,v_-,v_+\) and a common upper bound on \(\Delta_T\) that tends to zero.
statements.proof_tex:
Put
\[
 Q_T=T^{-1}\sum_{t=k_T+1}^T E_P[X_{T,t}^2\mid\mathcal G_{T,t-1}].
\]
Fix \(\eta>0\) and partition \([v_-,v_+]\) into finitely many Borel intervals \(I_r\) of diameter at most \(\eta\). The events \(B_r=\{\lambda_T\in I_r\}\) belong to \(\mathcal G_{T,k_T}\). Choose \(\lambda_r\in I_r\). For every cell of positive probability, let \(P_r=P(\,\cdot\mid B_r)\). Because \(B_r\in\mathcal G_{T,k_T}\subseteq\mathcal G_{T,t-1}\) for \(t>k_T\), the defining martingale-difference equality remains valid under \(P_r\):
\[
 E_{P_r}[X_{T,t}\mid\mathcal G_{T,t-1}]
 =\frac{E_P[\mathbf 1_{B_r}X_{T,t}\mid\mathcal G_{T,t-1}]}{P(B_r\mid\mathcal G_{T,t-1})}=0.
\]
Here the displayed ratio is read only on \(B_r\), where its denominator is one; equivalently, the equality follows directly by testing against bounded \(\mathcal G_{T,t-1}\)-measurable functions under the conditional law.

Define
\[
 d_r=E_{P_r}|Q_T-\lambda_T|+\eta,
 \qquad q_r=E_{P_r}Q_T,
 \qquad s_r^2=Tq_r.
\]
Since \(|\lambda_T-\lambda_r|\le\eta\) on \(B_r\),
\[
 |q_r-\lambda_r|\le d_r,
 \qquad
 \sum_rP(B_r)d_r\le\Delta_T+\eta.
\]
Call a cell good when \(d_r\le v_-/2\). The total probability of the bad cells is at most \(2(\Delta_T+\eta)/v_-\). On a good cell, \(q_r\ge v_-/2\), and the normalized predictable quadratic variation in the cited Mourrat bound is \(V_r^2=Q_T/q_r\). Therefore
\[
 E_{P_r}|V_r^2-1|
 \le q_r^{-1}E_{P_r}|Q_T-q_r|
 \le \frac{4d_r}{v_-}.
\]
The increments are bounded by \(L\), the number of tail increments is at most \(T\), and \(s_r^2\ge Tv_-/2\). Apply the cited quantitative bound \(\mathrm{lem:mourrat\text{-}bounded\text{-}martingale\text{-}clt}\) with \(p=1\) under \(P_r\). It gives a common constant \(C\) such that
\[
 \sup_z\left|P_r\left\{T^{-1/2}\sum_{t>k_T}X_{T,t}\le z\right\}
 -\Phi\left(\frac z{\sqrt{q_r}}\right)\right|
 \le C\left\{\frac{\log T}{\sqrt T}+\left(d_r+T^{-1}\right)^{1/3}\right\}
\]
on every good cell. The normal scale family is uniformly Lipschitz in its variance on \([v_-/2,2v_+]\): indeed, with \(\phi\) the standard normal density,
\[
 \sup_z\left|\frac{\partial}{\partial q}\Phi\left(\frac z{\sqrt q}\right)\right|
 =\sup_u\frac{|u|\phi(u)}{2q}\le C_{v_-}.
\]
Consequently, on a good cell,
\[
 \sup_z\left|\Phi\left(\frac z{\sqrt{q_r}}\right)
 -E_{P_r}\Phi\left(\frac z{\sqrt{\lambda_T}}\right)\right|
 \le C_{v_-}d_r.
\]
After multiplying by \(P(B_r)\), summing, bounding each bad-cell discrepancy by one, and using concavity of \(x^{1/3}\), we obtain
\[
 \sup_z\left|P\left\{T^{-1/2}\sum_{t>k_T}X_{T,t}\le z\right\}
 -E_P\Phi\left(\frac z{\sqrt{\lambda_T}}\right)\right|
 \le C\left\{\frac{\log T}{\sqrt T}+\left(\Delta_T+\eta+T^{-1}\right)^{1/3}
 +\Delta_T+\eta\right\}.
\]
Taking, for example, \(\eta=T^{-1}\) proves the assertion. Every constant in the display depends only on \(L,v_-,v_+\), which also proves the stated uniformity.

statements.statement: Let \(0<a\le b<\infty\), and let \((U_n)\) be random symmetric \(d\)-by-\(d\) matrices satisfying \(aI_d\preceq U_n\preceq bI_d\) almost surely. There are a subsequence \((n_k)\) and a Borel probability measure \(\mu\), supported on \(\mathcal K_{a,b}=\{u=u^\top:aI_d\preceq u\preceq bI_d\}\), such that \(E[f(U_{n_k})]\to\int f(u)\,d\mu(u)\) for every continuous \(f:\mathcal K_{a,b}\to\mathbb R\).
statements.proof_tex:
Identify a symmetric matrix with its \(s=d(d+1)/2\) upper-triangular entries. The set \(\mathcal K_{a,b}\) is closed and bounded in \(\mathbb R^s\), hence compact. For every integer \(r\ge1\), make a finite Borel partition \(\mathcal P_r\) of \(\mathcal K_{a,b}\) into sets of Euclidean diameter at most \(2^{-r}\), with \(\mathcal P_{r+1}\) refining \(\mathcal P_r\). Such partitions are obtained recursively by intersecting each cell with a finite \(2^{-r-2}\)-ball cover and disjointifying the intersections in a fixed order.

There are only countably many cells in \(\bigcup_r\mathcal P_r\). Since every cell probability belongs to \([0,1]\), successive subsequence selection followed by diagonal selection gives a subsequence, still denoted \((n_k)\), for which
\[
 \ell(C)=\lim_{k\to\infty}P\{U_{n_k}\in C\} \tag{1}
\]
exists for every partition cell \(C\). The limits are nonnegative, sum to one on each level, and are consistent under refinement. They therefore define a probability distribution on infinite nested cell paths: at a cell of positive mass choose a child with conditional probability \(\ell(C')/\ell(C)\), and assign arbitrary child probabilities after a zero-mass cell. Choose a point \(u_C\in C\) in every nonempty cell. Along every path of positive probability, the representatives are Cauchy because a level-\(r+1\) representative and all later representatives lie in the same level-\(r\) cell and hence are at distance at most \(2^{-r}\). Compactness gives a limit in \(\mathcal K_{a,b}\). Let \(U\) be this limit and let \(\mu\) be its law. Consistency makes the path probability of a level-\(r\) cell equal to \(\ell(C)\).

Let \(f\) be continuous. Compactness makes it uniformly continuous; write
\[
 \omega_f(h)=\sup\{|f(u)-f(v)|:u,v\in\mathcal K_{a,b},\ \|u-v\|_2\le h\},
 \qquad \omega_f(h)\downarrow0. \tag{2}
\]
For one representative \(u_C\) per cell,
\[
 \left|E[f(U_{n_k})]-\sum_{C\in\mathcal P_r}f(u_C)P\{U_{n_k}\in C\}\right|
 \le\omega_f(2^{-r}), \tag{3}
\]
and the same inequality holds with \(U\) and \(\ell(C)\). First let \(k\to\infty\) in the finite sum using (1), and then let \(r\to\infty\) using (2)--(3). This proves \(E[f(U_{n_k})]\to E[f(U)]=\int f\,d\mu\).

statements.statement: In the setting of Theorem 3, suppose the limiting covariance law has finite support \(\mu=\sum_{j=1}^r p_j\delta_{W_j}\), where \(r<\infty\), every \(p_j>0\), \(\sum_jp_j=1\), and every \(W_j\) is positive definite. For a fixed nonzero \(c\), the deterministic sandwich \(\Sigma\) has asymptotic coverage \(1-\alpha\) at every \(\alpha\in(0,1)\) if and only if \(c^\top W_jc=c^\top\Sigma c\) for every \(j\). The same \(\Sigma\) is valid at every level for every nonzero contrast if and only if \(W_j=\Sigma\) for every \(j\).
statements.proof_tex:
For the finite law in the statement and every Borel set \(B\),
\[
 \mu(B)=\sum_{j=1}^rp_j\mathbf1\{W_j\in B\}.
\tag{1}
\]
Because every \(p_j\) is strictly positive, a scalar equality \(c^\top Vc=c^\top\Sigma c\) holds \(\mu\)-almost surely if and only if it holds at every \(W_j\). Theorem \(\mathrm{thm:contrastwise\text{-}deterministic\text{-}sandwich\text{-}iff}\) therefore gives the first equivalence. Likewise, \(V=\Sigma\) holds \(\mu\)-almost surely if and only if every \(W_j=\Sigma\); Theorem \(\mathrm{thm:matrixwise\text{-}deterministic\text{-}sandwich\text{-}iff}\) gives the second equivalence. Thus the finite-support conclusion is a corollary of the covariance-law characterization.

statements.statement:
Consider the bounded-noise Guo--Xu recursion with arbitrary fixed \(\sigma_1,\sigma_2>0\) and deterministic tie arm \(1\). Put \(p=99/100\), \(q=1/100\), and, for \((u,v)\in[q,p]^2\), define
\[
 h(u,v)=\left(\frac{u+16v}{2},\frac{17-u-16v}{2},
                 \frac{u-4v}{4},\frac{-3-u+4v}{24}\right).
\]
For \(t\ge1\), put \(D_{t,a}=\Phi^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,a}\), \(N_{t,a}=b^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,a}\), and \(\Psi_t=(D_{t,1}/t,D_{t,2}/t,N_{t,1}/t,N_{t,2}/t)\). Then \(q^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,a}=O(t^{-1})\) almost surely, \(\Psi_t\) obeys an exact stochastic-approximation recursion with step \(1/(t+1)\), and its affine interpolation is a bounded perturbed solution, hence an asymptotic pseudotrajectory, of the closed convexified inclusion \(\dot\psi\in F(\psi)\) below. Writing \(\Delta(\psi)=n_1/d_1-n_2/d_2\), \(h_+=h(p,q)\), \(h_-=h(q,p)\), \(h_1=h(p,p)\), and \(h_2=h(q,q)\), its graph on \(d_1,d_2>0\) is
\[
 F(\psi)=
 \begin{cases}
  \{h_+-\psi\},&\Delta(\psi)>0,\\
  \{h_--\psi\},&\Delta(\psi)<0,\\
  \operatorname{co}\{h_+,h_-,h_1\}-\psi,&\Delta(\psi)=0,\ d_1<d_2,\\
  \operatorname{co}\{h_+,h_-,h_2\}-\psi,&\Delta(\psi)=0,\ d_1>d_2,\\
  \operatorname{co}\{h_+,h_-,h_1,h_2\}-\psi,&\Delta(\psi)=0,\ d_1=d_2.
 \end{cases}
\]
Every almost-sure normalized-state limit set is internally chain transitive for \(F\) and is contained in the computable parallelogram \(\mathcal C=\{h(u,v):(u,v)\in[q,p]^2\}\); the projected slope limit set is its continuous image under \((d_1,d_2,n_1,n_2)\mapsto(n_1/d_1,n_2/d_2)\).

The smaller inclusion having only \(h_+-\psi\), \(h_--\psi\), and \(\operatorname{co}\{h_+-\psi,h_--\psi\}\) on the switching surface is not a valid unconditional reduction of this recursion. If it were the limiting inclusion, its only internally chain-transitive sets would be the three singletons \(\{h_-\}\), \(\{h(u_0,1-u_0)\}\), and \(\{h_+\}\), where
\[
 u_0=\frac{47+\sqrt{4609}}{150},\qquad
 \frac{N_1}{D_1}=\frac{N_2}{D_2}
 =b_0:=\frac{\sqrt{4609}-91}{1224}
 \quad\text{at }h(u_0,1-u_0).
\]
The correct graph instead has an uncountable family of additional internally chain-transitive singleton equilibria. Explicitly, for
\[
 u\in[u_0,p],\qquad
 v(u)=\frac{3u+18-\sqrt{25u^2-228u+324}}{32},
\]
one has \(h(u,v(u))\in\mathcal C\), equal slope coordinates, first normalized Gram coordinate smaller than the second, and \(0\in F(h(u,v(u)))\). In particular,
\[
 v_*:=v(p)=\frac{2097}{3200}-\frac{3\sqrt{5457}}{640}
\]
gives an equilibrium \(h(p,v_*)\) distinct from \(h_-\), \(h(u_0,1-u_0)\), and \(h_+\). This continuum is an explicit internally-chain-transitive obstruction to a three-candidate conclusion from the standard differential-inclusion route.

For the actual recursion, on \(\mathcal L_+=\{\liminf_t(\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,1}-\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,2})>0\}\) and \(\mathcal L_-=\{\limsup_t(\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,1}-\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,2})<0\}\), respectively,
\[
 (\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,1},\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,2})^\top
 \longrightarrow
 \left(\frac{19}{46},-\frac{79}{3804}\right)^\top
 \quad\text{and}\quad
 \left(-\frac{79}{634},\frac{19}{276}\right)^\top.
\]
Both events have probability bounded away from zero uniformly over \(\eta_0\in\mathsf K_{\mathrm{GX}}\), and the corresponding pathwise Cesaro errors converge to zero. If both slopes have a common-coordinate subsequential limit and \((u,v)\) is a simultaneous subsequential limit of the empirical conditional arm-\(1\) rates, then necessarily
\[
 u^2+12uv-21u-64v^2+72v=0.
\]
The relation \(v=1-u\), and hence the candidate \((u_0,b_0)\), is justified only if same-arm switching-layer occupation is separately excluded; the exact recursion does not provide that exclusion. Consequently, this argument proves neither finite almost-sure tail selection nor zero probability of switching-surface convergence. It also proves no compact-initial-set uniform attraction moduli \(r_T(K_0),\delta_T(K_0)\). These are dynamics-only conclusions: they assert neither membership in \(\mathfrak P_T\) nor applicability of any inference theorem.
statements.justification: The normalized sufficient-statistic recursion gives the strongest rigorous dynamics certificate currently available: it proves the two separated limits and exposes an uncountable switching-equilibrium obstruction in the correct limiting differential inclusion.
statements.gap: The differential-inclusion limit set need not be one of three candidates because the vanishing UCB bonus produces same-arm modes inside the shrinking switching layer. Actual selection within that layer, zero probability of switching convergence, and compact-initial-set uniform attraction still require quantitative escape and equicontinuity estimates not supplied here.
statements.consumer: The result prevents the bounded Guo--Xu analogue from being used as a certified two-basin inference witness while identifying the exact normalized-state graph and the additional dynamics that a future separatrix analysis must control.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Saco's Theorem 5.14 gives pointwise realized-QV Studentized inference for its logged-propensity martingale AIPW/DML setup. The present theorem verifies uniform realized-to-predictable QV control, exact-root localization, truncation inactivity, feasible inverse control, and coverage for the bounded finite-attractor IPW-Z class. The two published hypothesis and estimator classes are non-nested, so no strict theorem-level tightening is claimed.

Scaled inverse-propensity convergence yields ordinary Gaussian IPW-Z inference. Pointwise limiting-policy convergence implies the present Cesaro condition only after suitable common-envelope and rate strengthening, and the numerical two-mode example does not prove those uniform conditions.
Directional stability suffices for target-specific efficient normal inference and is weaker than target-agnostic matrix stability.
For generalized Gaussian Thompson sampling, a continuous-state SDE invariant law controls optimal-arm pull proportions and nonstandard normalized-mean limits in the multiple-optimum regime.

Off-policy M-estimation under working-model misspecification targets a projected solution under a stationary evaluation policy and uses flexible variance stabilization under unstable logging policies.

Conditional on entering an attraction domain, stochastic approximation locks into a prescribed stable equilibrium with an explicit high-probability bound; this does not by itself provide the present compact-uniform Cesaro modulus for a terminal random representative.

tldr: The field-tier contribution is a conditional finite-attractor theorem bundle for adaptive causal IPW-Z inference. Under common score, derivative, Jacobian-lower-bound, policy, covariance-lower-bound, root-separation, attraction, and local root-search envelopes, with attainable basins defined as the positive-mass support of the tail selector, the bundle derives a basin-stable finite Gaussian mixture with predictable-QV error controlled by \(r_T+\delta_T\), proves that an always-defined same-path realized-QV sandwich is uniformly pivotal and asymptotically untruncated, and gives exact deterministic-sandwich boundaries: every-level validity for one contrast holds if and only if that contrast's variance is basin-invariant, while validity for all contrasts holds if and only if the full covariance is deterministic. Theorem 2 has one direct strict-tightening comparator, Saco's pointwise realized-QV result; the remaining named papers provide motivation, ingredients, or orthogonal regimes rather than a second strict frontier. An elementary bounded two-basin law verifies that contrastwise invariance need not imply matrix invariance. The slope-projected limit set of the augmented bounded Guo--Xu Markov chain remains an open dynamics question with no class-membership or inference claim.

project_justification.gap: Saco supplies the one direct pointwise realized-QV comparator, but not uniform verification over an endogenous finite-attractor class. Guo--Xu and Shen and coauthors supply adjacent stable-policy and directional-stability results, Han studies continuous SDE-invariant Thompson-sampling pull proportions and raw-arm-mean inference, and Leiner, Dunn, and Ramdas study stationary-evaluation-policy off-policy M-estimation with flexible variance stabilization under unstable logging. Zhang, Janson, and Murphy instead study pooled longitudinal adaptive sampling with Z-estimation and an adaptive sandwich estimator in a fixed-within-user, growing-participant regime. Existing stochastic-approximation results control lock-in only after entry into an attraction domain, and the Guo--Xu two-mode example remains numerical.
project_justification.niche: The unoccupied field-tier object is a conditional recursion-level uniform limit theory that preserves the random basin, validates a finite-sample-defined same-path studentizer, and states exact contrastwise and matrixwise boundaries for deterministic-sandwich inference. The absence of a second direct strict-tightening comparator caps the positioning at field tier, which is the requested floor and achieved target.
project_justification.fill: The publishable contribution is the conditional finite-attractor theorem bundle: a basin-stable causal IPW-Z finite Gaussian mixture, a uniformly feasible same-path realized-QV pivot, and exact contrastwise and matrixwise deterministic-sandwich boundaries. A finite-attractor class indexed by common score, derivative, Jacobian lower, policy, covariance lower, root-separation, attraction, and local root-search envelopes converts policy dynamics into predictable-QV control with error \(r_T+\delta_T\); its attainable-basin index set is the positive-mass support of the tail selector. The score and derivative envelopes already imply \(\Omega_j\preceq(KB^2/\varepsilon)I_d\) and \(\|H\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le KD_1\), so no primitive upper matrix bounds are imposed. The proposal-specific envelope \(e_T=T^{-1/2}+r_T+\delta_T\) combines sampling, attraction, and approximation errors. A preliminary moment-norm minimizer localizes a compact empirical-root set; martingale concentration and a quantitative inverse-function argument make the exact-root selector active with probability tending uniformly to one. Stable martingale convergence supplies the mixture, event-truncated realized QV supplies the feasible pivot, finite normal-mixture identification plus polarization supplies the two necessity results, and a bounded in-class law certifies strict logical separation of the directional and matrix frontiers.

related_work: Guo and Xu, Theorems 3.2--3.3, prove marginal and joint IPW-Z Gaussian limits after scaled inverse propensities stabilize; their Section 3.1 no-intercept clipped-LinUCB example supplies numerical evidence of two modes, not a proved finite-attractor theorem or certification of the present class. Guo--Xu is an informed-by comparator. Saco, Theorem 5.14 and Design A in Section 6.6, establishes a pointwise realized-QV pivot under variance growth and illustrates random post-burn-in variance; Theorem 2 is the sole direct strict tightening, giving uniform validity over the conditional finite-attractor class and deriving truncation inactivity from common basin-covariance, attraction, and exact-root localization controls. The Abstract and Introduction of Shen and coauthors distinguish directional stability from full-matrix stability; that distinction informs Theorems 3--4, while the finite-basin every-level converses and bounded separation witness are not presented as a strict comparator chain. Han studies an orthogonal instability mechanism and target: for generalized Gaussian Thompson sampling, Proposition 2.6 and Theorem 2.7 on PDF pages 9--10, together with introduction equation (1.4) on page 4, identify the joint optimal-arm pull-proportion and noise limit with the unique invariant law of a continuous-state SDE. Han's Theorem 3.2 on PDF page 12 and introduction equation (1.5) on page 5 give Gaussian normalized-mean limits for stable arms and an SDE-defined semi-universal limit for multiple optimal arms; the body reports simulation evidence that the latter law is genuinely non-Gaussian, and Corollary 3.3 on PDF page 13 constructs confidence intervals from its quantiles. Han is close motivation, not a result anticipating Theorems 1--4 or the bounded Guo--Xu certification question. Leiner, Dunn, and Ramdas study off-policy M-estimation under working-model misspecification for adaptively collected bandit data. Their target is a projected solution under a stationary evaluation policy, and flexible variance stabilization permits unstable or nonconvergent logging policies; this is an informed-by comparator rather than a same-path-QV or finite-attractor result. Borkar supplies local lock-in bounds, and Pemantle supplies unstable-point avoidance, but neither certifies the bounded recursion. Aldous and Eagleson supply stable-convergence language. Mourrat supplies only the bounded-martingale central-limit and quadratic-variation ingredient. Teicher together with Andrews and Mallows supplies identification of centered normal scale mixtures. Qian and coauthors and Liao and coauthors define the HeartSteps causal-excursion consumer. Zhang, Janson, and Murphy study pooled longitudinal adaptive sampling with Z-estimation and an adaptive sandwich estimator in a fixed-within-user, growing-participant regime. Thus the comparison supports a field-tier conditional theorem bundle, with Saco as its only strict-tightening comparator and no second strict frontier.
technical_internal_limitation: The two slopes do not form a Markov state because clipped-UCB decisions also depend on the inverse ridge Gram coordinates. The open-ended question therefore concerns the slope projection of the augmented chain \(Z^{\mathrm{GX}}_t\) on \(\mathsf E_{\mathrm{GX}}\); \(\mathsf K_{\mathrm{GX}}\) indexes only its initial slopes and is not an invariant chain state space. This bounded Rademacher recursion is not yet shown to have finite projected tail selection, a relative-basin-interior Cesaro attraction modulus, or any separately specified causal-score structure, so it is not claimed to belong to \(\mathfrak P_T\) and Theorems 1--2 are not claimed to apply. Optional Gaussian moment-extension subquestion: after the bounded-model dynamics are classified, determine whether the published Gaussian-noise recursion admits analogous dynamics under suitable moment controls. This optional subquestion is not a premise, deliverable, theorem, or part of the bounded-model open-ended question. Correct coverage at one isolated nominal level also does not identify the scale mixture: two unequal basin variances can be paired with a deterministic scale whose symmetric interval has the desired probability at that one level. Theorem 3 deliberately requires every nominal level.
honest_scope: The project establishes a field-tier inference frontier conditional on membership in the common-envelope finite-attractor class. Saco is the only direct strict-tightening comparator; the absence of a second direct strict frontier caps the contribution at field tier, which is the requested floor and achieved target. Guo--Xu, Shen and coauthors, Han, Leiner--Dunn--Ramdas, Borkar, and the remaining cited papers serve as informed-by comparators, ingredients, close motivation, or orthogonal regimes. The project treats a growing-horizon superpopulation adaptive experiment with a known randomization rule, not a pure fixed-finite-population randomization theorem. The bounded two-basin construction is solely an elementary, non-novel existence witness for strict logical separation between contrastwise and matrixwise invariance. It is not evidence that either the specified bounded Rademacher analogue or the published Gaussian no-intercept Guo--Xu recursion satisfies the finite-attractor, attraction, or common-envelope conditions. The open-ended question concerns only the slope-projected dynamics of the augmented bounded chain and does not assert membership in \(\mathfrak P_T\) or applicability of Theorems 1--2. Any future inference theorem must separately specify its causal score, parameter space, unique target root, nonzero target contrast, induced scalar target, and every class assumption. The Gaussian moment extension remains optional and open. When \(m=1\), \(J=1\), \(V_J=V_1\) is deterministic, Theorem 1 is ordinary asymptotic normality, Theorem 2 is ordinary realized-QV studentization, and Theorems 3--4 allow \(\Sigma=V_1\).
